dossier.public_summary: The light curve shows a shallow dip followed by a much deeper dip at the same folded period, with a V-shaped transit and strong starspot variability. Depth inconsistency and the odd/even difference point to an eclipsing binary or blended stellar eclipse rather than a 1.9 Earth-radius planet, and the depth ratio is much larger than expected for a planet.

reasons.why: Strong odd/even difference suggests binary at twice the folded period; not consistent with a single planet period.
Three transits have inconsistent depths, driven by a shallow odd transit versus a deep even transit, positive evidence for two different eclipses / blended binary, not measurement scatter.
Transit shape is V-shaped (approaching significance), favours grazing binary over flat-bottomed planet, combined with odd/even and depth scatter.

Star is a heavily spotted rotator (Teff 5140, K dwarf) with variability amplitude several times the transit depth; V-shape plus shallow/deep alternation is typical of spot-induced or ellipsoidal binary signal, not a transiting planet.
No on-target centroid to rule out a neighbour, but no improvement for planet case either; favoured blend/EB on target remains viable, planet_rank 0.1 supports low planet score.
